title: Completing a polynomial presentation preserves its conormal differential
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $S=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $\alpha:S\twoheadrightarrow B$ a surjective homomorphism of commutative $A$-algebras with finitely generated kernel $K$. Write $P=\varprojlim_n S/I^nS$ and $\widehat B=\varprojlim_n B/I^nB$ for the adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $\widehat\alpha:P\to\widehat B$ be the map induced by $\alpha$ on compatible sequences. Then $\widehat\alpha$ is surjective, its kernel is $J=KP$ (the ideal generated by the image of $K$), and the canonical map $(K/K^2)\otimes_B\widehat B\to J/J^2$, $\bar k\otimes b\mapsto b\bar k$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Polynomial differentiation [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] induces continuous partial derivatives on $P$ by differentiating each coordinate modulo $I^nS$. The maps $d_0:K/K^2\to B^{\oplus r}$, $\bar f\mapsto(\alpha(\partial f/\partial x_i))_i$, and $\widehat d:J/J^2\to\widehat B^{\oplus r}$, $\bar f\mapsto(\widehat\alpha(\partial f/\partial x_i))_i$, are well-defined linear maps over $B$ and $\widehat B$, respectively. Under the displayed conormal isomorphism and the canonical identification $B^{\oplus r}\otimes_B\widehat B\cong\widehat B^{\oplus r}$, one has $\widehat d=d_0\otimes_B\widehat B$.

source.place: Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), statement and proof: completion is exact on finite modules, the completed presentation has kernel K^wedge=KP, and (K/K^2) tensor_B B^wedge = K^wedge/(K^wedge)^2; equation-NL specifies the continuous partial-derivative differential.
